newsitem.title: USA: Corn rootworm-resistant seed in pipeline -Novartis.
newsitem.headline: Corn rootworm-resistant seed in pipeline -Novartis.

text.p: Novartis Seeds Inc hopes to have a genetically-engineered seed with resistance to the corn rootworm on the market at the turn of the century, company official Dr. Mark Wall said Saturday.

"This is a big opportunity. If we can pull this off, if we're as successful with corn rootworm as we were with Bt (corn), this would be a big deal for corn growers," Wall said at the annual joint convention of the American Soybean Association and the National Corn Growers Association.
Novartis Seeds is in a race with other companies to produce a biotech product for the pest, he said.
Wall estimated U.S. corn growers spend about $130 million a year to control rootworm.
Researchers developed Bt corn, which is resistant to the European corn borer, first because it was easier scientifically. Bt corn provides a genetic springboard to a corn rootworm product, Wall said.
